what: The recipes whose owner or rank is a decision rather than a reading, which scripts\dev\Build-RecipeTable.ps1 reads as RECIPE_OWNER and RECIPE_RANK. Each entry carries the measured reason it cannot be derived, and the reason lands on the row in game\data\recipes.json. No script writes this file: it is changed by hand, in a pull request, with the recipe it names (#3470).
why: Data, not code: a recipe change is the content plugin and this file, so the box's Rebuild-ContentTables can rebuild a pull request's tables with main's own builders and only these two files taken from it (Patrick, 30 Oct 2026, B on the report page).

ThornswoodRecipeToolShovel.Why: a shovel is a tool a smith forges, and it is here rather than derived because Shovel01 is a MISC: the forge settles ownership by the output being a WEAP, so the pickaxe and the axe are covered by that rule and the shovel is not. Patrick, 21 September: a broken tool is replaced by "a smith making them".

ThornswoodRecipeKeyMold.Why: a key mold is a smith's work and it is here for the same reason the shovel is: the output is a MISC, so the forge rule, which settles ownership by the output being a WEAP, cannot see it. Patrick, 23 September: "make a fucking mold item craftable dude this would solve alot".

ThornswoodRecipeKey.Why: a key is cut by a smith off a stamped mold, and the mold is checked server side in mp.onCraft rather than as an input, because an input is taken by the engine and Patrick asked for the mold to be reusable: "it can be reused". Same MISC output as the mold, so the same reason it cannot be derived.

ThornswoodRecipeWeaponKit.Why: the Weapon Kit is the Edgewright's repair kit (docs/systems/durability.md), and the output is a MISC, so the forge rule, which settles ownership by the output being a WEAP, cannot see it. Patrick, 4 October: use a suggested recipe; this is the one picked (#1384).

ThornswoodRecipeArmorKit.Why: the Armor Kit is the Platewright's repair kit (docs/systems/durability.md). A MISC at a forge, so the forge rule cannot see it, and it would not land on the Platewright if it could. Patrick, 4 October: use a suggested recipe; this is the one picked (#1384).

ThornswoodRecipeSewingKit.Why: the Sewing Kit is the Haberdasher's repair kit (docs/systems/durability.md). A MISC at the tanning rack, which is open furniture whose own rule hands a hide into leather to the Platewright, so nothing derived would give it to a tailor. Patrick, 4 October: use a suggested recipe; this is the one picked (#1384).

ThornswoodRecipeBandage.Why: the bandage is a tailor's work (docs/systems/injury.md, who treats what). Patrick, 4 October, on #1383: a Haberdasher novice recipe at the loom. A MISC, named here so its half is that answer and not a reading of the output.

ThornswoodRecipeSplint.Why: the splint holds a break (docs/systems/injury.md). Patrick, 4 October, on #1383: a Woodwright novice recipe at the kiln. The kiln's own rule gives its work to the Charburner, so it is named here.

ThornswoodRecipePoultice.Why: the poultice cuts the wound fever chance (docs/systems/injury.md). Patrick, 4 October, on #1383: a Physicker recipe at novice. A MISC at the alchemy lab Thornswood-Content.esp ships, a create-object bench, which nothing else names.

ThornswoodRecipeRemedy.Why: the physicker's remedy closes a cut and clears one ordinary disease (docs/systems/injury.md, disease.md, physicker.md). Patrick, 4 October, on #1383: a Physicker recipe at advanced, which its blue mountain flower makes it. A MISC at the same alchemy lab.

ThornswoodRecipeFishTrap.Why: the fish trap is a woodwright novice good, made with the poles (docs/systems/classes/fisher.md, issue #1379). A MISC at a forge with no pole in its name, so neither the forge rule nor the spear rule can see it.

ThornswoodRecipeToolHammer.Why: the hammer is the smith's own tool (#3162), forged like the pickaxe, the axe and the shovel from an iron ingot and a handle. A MISC, so the forge rule cannot see it. The one forge row that asks for no hammer (benchToolKey in game/gamemode.js), so a smith whose hammer broke can make another.

ThornswoodRecipeToolShears.Why: the tailor's shears (#3162). A smith forges a tailor's tool as a smith forges a miner's pickaxe: a tool is a smith's work (Patrick, 21 September: a broken tool is replaced by "a smith making them"). A MISC, so the forge rule cannot see it.

ThornswoodRecipeToolAlembic.Why: the alchemist's alembic (#3162), forged from two iron ingots for the same reason as the shears. A MISC, so the forge rule cannot see it.

ThornswoodRecipeToolRuneKnife.Why: the enchanter's rune knife (#3162), a blade and so an Edgewright's, forged from an iron ingot with a leather strip for the grip. A MISC, so the forge rule cannot see it.

ThornswoodRecipeToolLadle.Why: the cook's wooden ladle (#3162), Skyrim's WoodenLadle01, carved from firewood at the woodworking bench like the poles. A MISC with no pole in its name, so the spear rule cannot see it.
